title: Make Them Want to Follow You: The Law of Fickleness
coreMove: Establish authority through steadiness, fairness, and inner authority while follower demands shift and test you.
sourcePressure: This law studies the emotional contract between leader and followers: people want direction, resent dependence, test power, and withdraw respect when authority looks needy or unfair.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Making leadership a popularity lesson or command style instead of the unstable emotional contract authority must manage.

sourceAnchors.name: Queen Elizabeth I
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses Elizabeth as the central authority anchor, preserving symbolic weight and distance amid unstable public feeling
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Elizabeth keeps authority from becoming cheap by refusing to let the court fully possess her.

sourceAnchors.name: William Cecil and Mary Queen of Scots
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses Cecil as a support for preserved form and Mary as the contrast of exposed, entangled authority
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Cecil protects the form of power while Mary shows how exposed dependence makes authority easier to test.
